title: Lesson 4: BLESS - Serve with Loving Sacrifice
description: Before Jesus asked His friends to serve, He knelt and washed their feet. This lesson shows how Jesus served you first, why the last will be first in His kingdom, and how to climb down on purpose to lift your one up.

blocks.text: In Lessons 2 and 3 you prayed for your one, listened, and opened your table. Now comes the most hands-on rhythm of BLESS, Serve, where love stops only showing up and starts rolling up its sleeves.

blocks.alt: Jesus kneeling with a basin and a towel, washing the feet of His disciples at the Last Supper

blocks.title: The Towel and the Basin
blocks.text:
It was the night before the cross. Jesus knew exactly what was coming: Judas would betray Him, Peter would deny Him, and the rest would scatter. Nobody at the table had washed anyone's feet. It was the lowest job in the house, and no one wanted it.

"Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come from God and was going back to God, rose from supper. He laid aside his outer garments, and taking a towel, tied it around his waist. Then he poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples' feet." (John 13:3-5)

Peter could not stand it. "You shall never wash my feet." Jesus answered, "If I do not wash you, you have no part with me." When He was finished, He sat back down and said, "If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet." (John 13:14)

Jesus had every right to be served, but He chose to serve. He had hours left to live, and He spent them on dirty feet. That is the picture He wanted His followers to keep: not power, not status, but a towel and a basin.
Jesus Served You First

Before Jesus told anyone to wash feet, He washed theirs, and Peter nearly missed the whole point. "You shall never wash my feet," he said. Jesus answered, "If I do not wash you, you have no share with me" (John 13:8). You cannot lift anyone up until you let Jesus lift you.

That night was a small picture of something much bigger. Jesus climbed down into a pit you could never climb out of, your sin and the debt you owed a holy God, and He gave His life to pay what you could never pay.
He drew me up from the pit of destruction, out of the miry bog, and set my feet upon a rock, making my steps secure.

So you do not serve to earn your place with God. Your debt is paid and your feet are on the rock, so you are free to lift others up without needing them to lift you back. What you receive, you give away.
4.1 - What changes when you serve as someone Jesus has already served?
The Last Will Be First
A few days earlier, on the road to Jerusalem, Jesus told His disciples for the third time that He would die and rise again. Right away, two of them asked Him for something.

And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came up to him and said to him, "Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask of you." And he said to them, "What do you want me to do for you?" And they said to him, "Grant us to sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory."

They wanted the best seats, and the other ten were angry because they wanted them too. Underneath the seat is what every heart wants: to matter. So people climb, and they often step on others on the way up. Jesus gathered them all and turned the ladder upside down:

You know that those who are considered rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them. But it shall not be so among you. But whoever would be great among you must be your servant, and whoever would be first among you must be slave of all. For even the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.

In His kingdom, the last will be first. Greatness means climbing down to lift others up and leaving your own lifting to God. The world says, go get your title. Jesus says, go get your towel. And the towel comes with a title of its own. The world gives its titles to the people at the top, and every one of them fades. God gives His title to servants, and it lasts forever: "Well done, good and faithful servant" (Matthew 25:21).
4.2 - Where are you tempted to climb for a title instead of picking up the towel?
Lift Your One

Lifting someone up usually means climbing down on purpose into a hard place with them: a hospital room, a messy kitchen, a hard conversation. In His kingdom the question is not, "Who is serving me?" It is, "Who can I lift?" Your time, your skills, your money, your voice: God put them in your hands so you could lift someone up.

The most loving offers are specific. "Let me know if you need anything" is kind, but it hands the work back to the person who is already struggling. "Can I bring dinner Thursday?" or "I have Saturday morning free. Can I help with the yard?" gives them something easy to say yes to.
4.3 - What need have you heard from your one, and what is one specific way you could meet it?
This Week's Practice

Jesus asked James and John a servant's question: "What do you want me to do for you?" The King asked it first. This week, pray for your one by name and for the people under your own roof, then ask each of them: "How can I serve you this week?" Write down what they say, and follow through on at least one thing without needing anything back. If your one is not ready for that question yet, go back to Listen: ask, follow up, and remember.
Lesson 4 Review

On His last night, the King knelt with a towel and a basin. Jesus served you first, lifting you out of a pit you could never climb out of, so you serve from freedom, not for approval. What you receive, you give away. In His kingdom, the last will be first. The world says, go get your title. Jesus says, go get your towel. And one day, the Father will give you the only title that lasts: "Well done, good and faithful servant."
In the next lesson, you will learn the last rhythm, Story: how to share your own story and the story of Jesus with your one.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
